records.years: deputy governor of the National Bank of Cambodia, with the central bank 1979-1999; chaired the ACLEDA Bank board from 2000 until his retirement announced in October 2014
records.summary: ACLEDA Bank's own announcement of 16 October 2014, published on its group website, describes its retiring first chairman Chea Sok as "a former deputy-governor of the NBC" and says he "has led the Board since the transformation of ACLEDA to a registered bank in 2000". The bank's 2008 annual report sets out the central bank posts behind that description: from 1990 to 1999 he was Deputy Governor, Director of the Bank Supervision and Examination Department, Director of the Economic Research Department and General Director of the National Bank of Cambodia, and he joined the ACLEDA board in October 2000. So the official who had run bank supervision at the central bank went on to chair the board of a bank that supervision covers, for fourteen years. The employer is privately held: ACLEDA's own shareholder table, dated 20 August 2024, lists AFT 28.0564%, SMBC 18.0669%, public shareholders 17.6828%, COFIBRED 12.1271%, ORIX 12.1271%, shareholders legalized from ASA Plc. 5.7523%, NHTPE Rumdul 3.5000%, TMF 1.4485% and TFSF 1.2388%, with no government holding. ACLEDA began as an NGO and became a registered bank in 2000; it has not been state-owned, so no public-to-private handover sits between the shareholder table and his chairmanship.
records.source_title: ACLEDA Bank Plc., "Change of Chairman" announcement, 16 October 2014 (bank's own group website)

records.years: Executive President of Banco Multiple Promerica since 2017; board member since 2018; the central bank post is given with no dates
records.summary: Banco Multiple Promerica's own corporate governance report for the year 1 January to 31 December 2025 says of its Executive President, Carlos Julio Camilo Vincent, that he 'laboro en el Banco Central de la Republica Dominicana', working in the central bank's economic area. The report gives his bank post as 'Presidente Ejecutivo de Banco Multiple Promerica Republica Dominicana desde 2017', and lists him as a Vocal, an internal or executive member of the board, since 2018. It does not say which central bank post he held or in which years. The same report sets out who owns the bank: Promerica Financial Corporation holds 4,545,399,800.00 in common shares, or 89.21 per cent, with Ramiro Ortiz Mayorga and Edgar Zurcher Gurdian each holding one common share and preferred shareholders holding 10.79 per cent. No state body appears in the table.
records.source_title: Banco Multiple Promerica, Informe Anual de Gobierno Corporativo 2025

held.reason: Still no dates for David K.C. Quan's National Bank of Solomon Islands role, so the employer's ownership at the time cannot be fixed. CBSI's 2023 annual report prints his profile as 'DAVID K.C. QUAN, MBE., MAICD., FIML. (Non-Executive Member) since 31 August 2016' and lists 'Deputy Chairman, National Bank of Solomon Islands' among previous positions with no years, alongside 'Chairman, Solomon Islands National Provident Fund' and 'Chairman, Solomon Telekom'. CBSI's 2016 annual report profile of Quan does not mention NBSI at all, so the role predates 2016 and the report added it later. NBSI ownership moved repeatedly: Commonwealth Bank of Australia 51 and the government 49 from 1981; Bank of Hawaii bought the 51 per cent in 1994; Bank of Hawaii gave the 51 per cent back to the government in 2002, with the National Provident Fund on 49 per cent and three trusts on 17 per cent each; Bank South Pacific wholly acquired NBSI in 2007 and it now operates as Bank South Pacific. His concurrent SINPF chairmanship points to the window when the provident fund held the stake, which would make the employer public. Solomon Islands Government Gazettes on paclii would carry the dated board appointment: rms.paclii.org and pacliirms.paclii.org answered 403 to automated requests and pacliirms.austlii.edu.au gave curl code 000 twice, so those need a hand check.

Banco de Cochabamba S.A.'s ownership is still unstated and Jaime Valencia Valencia's roles are undated. ASFI's Libro Historia Tomo I was read for 'Banco de Cochabamba': the phrase does not appear, and the only relevant line, in the Introduccion's section on the 1960s, is 'En la decada de los sesenta se produjo una importante ampliacion de las entidades bancarias, con la autorizacion para el establecimiento de los bancos Comercial e Industrial, Credito Oruro, Cochabamba y Santa Cruz de la Sierra' - an authorisation to establish, with nothing on shareholders or private ownership. ASFI's Historia de la Supervision tomo I refused both fetch attempts with a client error and needs a hand check. UDAPE's Analisis Economico vol. 12 art. 02 and the IISEC paper Determinantes microeconomicos de la tasa de interes contain no mention of Cochabamba. The insurer Compania Boliviana de Seguros S.A. was searched for a shareholder or private-ownership statement with no result.
